title.narrative: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Development Program (Subprogram 2)

description.narrative: The subprogram will further strengthen the operating environment for small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) to become drivers of private sector-led, diversified economic growth and increase their resilience to economic shocks such as those triggered by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic. Reforms under the subprogram (and overall program) are grouped into four pillars: (i) diversifying formal bank and nonbank financial instruments; (ii) reducing the institutional costs of doing business; (iii) improving trade facilitation and digitalization; and (iv) aligning skills and market needs.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.
06 Dec 2023 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-support-small-and-medium-sized-enterprises-uzbekistan

1.1. To ensure effective and efficient governance of the public credit guarantee (PCG) scheme for SMEs: (i) Ministry of Economic Development and Poverty Reduction (MOEDPR), in accordance with Order No. 35 aligned the State Fund for Support of Entrepreneurial Activity (State Fund) with the World Bank's 16 principles for Partial Credit Guarantees (PCG) by a) operationalizing separate and more transparent accounting systems for the guarantee and interest compensation windows; b) operationalizing a transparent operational framework for the issuance and management of guarantees with clear eligibility and qualification criteria, and introducing climate change risk management considerations into the environment and social management system (ESMS) used for project screening; c) operationalizing an effective risk management framework with a risk-based pricing policy and transparent claims management process, and operationalizing a Management Information System with quarterly reporting, external audit and variance analysis against budgets; and (ii) Presidential Decree No. 6263 established an independent board of directors for the PCG which is now functioning.

1.2. To ensure that the State Fund expands PCGs to women's business, (i) Ministry of Finance (MOF) approved the allocation of SUM200 billion to the State Fund in the 2021 state budget, and further funds will be allocated on an annual basis on the demand of the State Fund to achieve issuance of at least 25% of new guarantees to women's businesses; and (ii) government approved a microenterprise-focused PCG product (with a higher guarantee ratio of 70%-75% and a low maximum loan amount cap of $20,000).

1.3. To expand access to finance by enabling the use moveable collateral, including accounts receivables and warehousing receipt financing, as security in financial contracts: (i) CBU abolished CBU Regulation 953 "On Procedures for conducting factoring operations by commercial banks on the territory of Uzbekistan," and (ii) CBU abolished in August 2021, the requirements (approved in 2000 under CBU Regulation No. 905) that constrained the effective used of moveable collateral in SME credit financing by commercial banks.

1.4. To (i) promote financial innovations (FinTech, crowdfunding, etc.) to support SME financing, (ii) promote non-collateral-based lending to SMEs by expanding credit-history information, and (iii) support development of the nonbank finance sector's ability to serve SMEs, CBU submitted for COM approval the Law on NonBank Credit Institutions and Microfinance Activities comprising: (i) legislative amendments allowing the creation of a regulatory sandbox, (ii) obligating leasing, and selected retail companies to provide credit-history information to the credit bureau, and (iii) defining the scope of services and governance principles of factoring organizations, microfinance institutions, and pawnshops and the corresponding regulatory role of the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (CBU).

1.5. To ensure effective regulation of PCGs Government adopted a resolution and instructed CBU to submit to the COM: (i) amendments to the Law on Central Bank expanding CBU's mandate to regulate and supervise PCG activities; and (ii) amendments to related laws and regulations to implement the expanded mandate of CBU (as in (a)).

1.6. To allow capital contributions by nongovernment entities such as International Financial Institutions (IFIs), commercial banks, and other private sector investors, Presidential Decree No. 292 amended the charter of the State Fund and transformed it into a Joint Stock Company with the expanded mandate to provide green finance products, and with at least 1 independent woman board member.

1.7. To reduce asymmetries in information between lenders and borrowers and enable better credit risk monitoring (by CBU), Presidential Decree PF-5992 “On the Strategy of banking system reforms of the Republic of Uzbekistan for 2020-2025” was adopted and the Action Plan (No. 02/1-1161) was implemented to improve the activity of credit bureaus.

1.8. To enable transparent access to risk capital by SMEs: (i) COM Resolution VMQ-684 “On measures of organizing National Venture Capital Fund UZVC” operationalized a National Venture Capital Fund (UzVC) with an initial capitalization of $1.5 million; (ii) UzVC adopted good practice-based “Operational Guideline (Investment Policy) of National Fund UZVC, 2022”; and (iii) COM approved an action plan to diversify the capital base (of UZVC) by June 2024, to include private sector participation.

1.9. Presidential Decree No. PF-62 and COM Resolution No. 615 adopted “On making amendments and additions to certain documents of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, and considering some of them invalid in connection with the adoption of the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan “On Non-Bank Credit Institutions and Microfinance,” and CBU adopted regulations (Reg, N3391, N3423, N2209-3, and N3411) to implement the Law On Non-Bank Credit Institutions and Microfinance Activities, approved under 1.4.

2.1. To streamline inter-agency coordination for SME support services and improve targeting of financial and non-financial support to SMEs, (i) COM adopted Resolution No. 77 “On establishing Entrepreneurship Development Agency (EDA) under MOEDPR” and implemented streamlining of SME government support services under focal agency EDA and Presidential Decree No. 4862 operationalized a dedicated unit within EDA (with at least 1 female technical staff) to collect and analyze sex-disaggregated SME data (finance, sectors, jobs, procurement, training needs, etc.); and (ii) COM adopted Resolution 217 “On approval of the regulation on the order of providing compensation for procurement of energy saving and energy efficient technologies, as well as interest rate compensation on loans issued for these purposes out of the funds of the state budget of the Republic of Uzbekistan” and MOF implemented incentive mechanisms for SMEs to finance renewable-energy based and other green technologies.

2.2. To incentivize formalization of SMEs including through less onerous reporting requirements for SMEs, (i) Government adopted Resolution No. 6029 and consolidated personal income tax, corporate income tax and payroll tax into a single unified tax and reduced the unified tax rate for SMEs and large firms; and (ii) Government adopted Resolution No. 4611 “On additional measures for implementation of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)” mandating MOF as the agency responsible for the sequenced implementation of IFRS for SMEs.

2.3. To ensure effective targeting of financial and non-financial support to SMEs, MOEF submitted for Parliament approval a draft Entrepreneurship Code to operationalize the use of a consistent SME definition, including for women's businesses, based on international norms and practices.

2.4. To spur competition and regional employment (via SMEs), Government adopted Law on Public Procurement ZRU-684, Presidential Resolution No. 357 (including a Road Map “On further improvement of the field of information and communication technologies in 2022-2023”), Presidential Decree PF-21 and COM Decree VMQ-276 and: (i) implemented e-procurement for tenders including small-value tenders; (ii) implemented reservation of at least 5% of its small value IT contracts for SMEs developing digital solutions for small businesses, and (iii) rolled out a training program on the International Accounting Standard Board's (IASB) ‘IFRS for SMEs' commencing February 2022 to at least 50 SMEs, to increase SMEs accounting and financial management capacity.

2.5. To reduce administrative costs to SMEs of dispersed and duplicating government financial support schemes, Presidential Decree PF-269 “On measures of implementing administrative reforms of New Uzbekistan” and Presidential Decree PF-27 “On the State Program for the implementation of the new Uzbekistan Development Strategy for 2022-2026” streamlined (e.g., by clustering, closing, improving existing mechanisms, etc.) all SME financial support schemes under the SME Department (MOEF) by 2022.

3.1. To lower transaction costs for firms including SMEs (by reducing customs release times), government adopted Resolution “On the cardinal improvement of state management in the field of technical regulation” and the Agency for Technical Regulation implemented risk-based control over conformity of imported products.

3.2. To increase and diversify exports to the European Union (and increase overall export revenue), COM fully complied with the economic and governance requirements of the European Union's Generalized System of Preferences plus (GSP+) trade beneficiary status.

3.3. To catalyze local ICT SMEs and support digitalization of SMEs to implement the Government Decree “On approval of the strategy Digital Uzbekistan - 2030 and measures for its effective implementation,” (i) EDA implemented Resolution No. 5088 “About measures for the organization of activities of youth industrial and entrepreneurial zones, and also support of entrepreneurial initiatives of youth” and provided interest subsidies on loans to develop digital tools and online platforms for SMEs (e.g., digital applications for business -to- business, supply chain, optimization of search engines, crowdfunding, early warning mobile apps for agricultural SMEs, etc.); and (ii) Ministry of Information and Communications Technology implemented Resolution No. UP-6079 “On approval of the strategy “Digital Uzbekistan - 2030” and measures for its effective implementation” by operationalizing 133 regional digital competency training centers with women or women entrepreneurs constituting at least 25% of the trainees.

3.4. To overcome and reduce institutional and technical barriers to SMEs' export development, COM resolution No. 790 “On measures of organizing the activity of the Central Customs Laboratory (Tashkent) of the State Customs Committee” operationalized the high capacity customs clearance center, the laboratory received international accreditation (O'ZAK.SL.0128) and implemented ISO/IEC 17025-2019 requirements (for identification of textile products, a key exports sector with industries that predominantly employ women).

3.5. To develop the export industry and improve product quality, the government adopted the Law On Standardization (ZRU-800), the Law On Technical Regulation (ZRU-819, and the Law On accreditation of conformity assessment bodies (ZRU-820), and implemented the: (i) harmonization of the national system of technical regulation, standardization, certification and metrology with international norms, and (ii) the COM Resolution N43 “On approval of the list of conformity assessment objects that need conformity approval in the Republic of Uzbekistan” optimized the list of products (3,400) subject to sanitary and epidemiological examination.

3.6. To facilitate uptake of digitalization and electronic and digital financial services by SMEs, (i) Government adopted the (new) Law On electronic commerce (No. 792); (ii) CBU Resolution No. 3431 “On approval of the regulation on the procedure for licensing the activities of payment system operators and payment organizations” aligned ecommerce implementation rules (with the new Law on ecommerce) with the Law on Payments and Payments Systems (approved September 2019); and (iii) CBU Resolution No. 3434 “On approval of the regulation on the procedure for monitoring the activities of payment system operators and payment organizations” adopted regulations based on the Law “On Payments and Payment System.''.

3.7. To accelerate the overall digitalization environment for the population including SMEs, CBU adopted Resolution no. 1545-5 “On the procedure for making electronic payments through the interbank payment system” and implemented the policy on online payment for all state mandatory payments including duties, fees, and fines in accordance with President Decree No. RP-6079 “On approval of the strategy Digital Uzbekistan - 2030.”

4.1. To increase employability through industry-focused technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and in accordance with the Law on Employment No. 642 and Presidential Decree No. 1066, (i) Ministry of Employment and Labor Relations (MOELR) issued internal Order and earmarked SUM44.5 billion for skills training in 2021 under the State Employment Promotion Fund; (ii) MOELR accredited 14 new regional non-government skills training centers for women and youth with prospective industry employers involved in training and assessment; and (iii) MOELR incentivized annual skills training programs starting 2021, through 70% training cost reimbursement from the State Unemployment Fund.

4.2. To ensure uninterrupted funding for skills training programs: (i) MOEF implemented the “Law on State Budget for 2022 (ZRU-742) and the “Law on State Budget for 2023 (ZRU-813) and budgeted SUM 759 million ($62 million) and SUM 490 million ($40 million) for the State Employment Fund; and (ii) the Fund implemented Presidential Resolution PP-4804 “On additional measures to attract to entrepreneurship, increase labor activity and professional training of poor and unemployed people, as well as ensure employment” for skills development, including through monocentresi for key sectors of the economy (such as banking, agro-industry, textiles, food processing, machine building, metallurgy, and chemicals), and with KPIs linked to 1.11, and ensured at least 30% women participation.

4.3. To increase employability and ensure industry feedback for improvement of training programs, (i) Agency of Statistics and the Center for Economic Research and Reforms implemented Presidential Resolution PP-4796 “On measures for further improvement and development of national system of statistics” (Chapter 8) and respectively, (i) conducted quarterly enterprise surveys and completed the first survey by in 2022, and (ii) conducted monthly monitoring of the state of business activity at the regional level. (ii) MOEDPR developed and implemented annually, including beyond 2023, at least 10 training programs on IASB's IFRS for SMEs for accountants and at least 10 training programs on SME digitalization and green technologies.
